metadataReview.note: The catalogued event is the dawn attack on the town of Kittanning on 8 September 1756, not the expedition's marches. The Pennsylvania marker record states that Kittanning, the most notable Delaware town west of the Alleghenies, was situated at the marker site until Armstrong's expedition destroyed it, and its narrative dates the surprise dawn raid to 8 September 1756. The locator is the marker position, used as a town-site reference for the attack; the approach and return marches are not represented. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses, captives and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: ExplorePAHistory's record for the Kittanning marker dedicated on 28 November 1946 (S. Water St. and west end of the Market St. Bridge) embeds the map position latitude 40.81358 and longitude -79.52127, rounded to [-79.5213,40.8136]. The marker text says the Delaware town was 'situated here'. GeoNames 5196357 places present Kittanning about 0.3 km north at 40.81645, -79.52199. This is a roadside marker for the town site, not a surveyed village boundary or any troop position. No accuracy radius is claimed.
